VA-2026-HB1007.s: Virginia changed rules for its birth-injury compensation program and fund. It allows electronic claim filing, sends related civil cases to the Workers' Compensation Commission, and adds some board, audit, bonding, and monthly meeting rules. It also raises the amount that may be awarded to families from $100,000 to $500,000 and is effective July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB1007.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB101.s: The law changes how people can submit an application for a concealed handgun permit. It removes the rule that the application must be filed in writing, which can allow other ways to submit it. It became law and takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB101.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB1011.s: The law lets local governments give a local compost product the tie-breaker in bidding for compost and similar soil amendment products they buy. It also lets a locality require some large waste generators to sort out organic waste, keep it out of final disposal, and face civil penalties after a warning. It also says new public school buildings and major changes should include trash, recycling, food scraps, and liquid waste disposal spaces. It became law and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB1011.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB1015.s: The law bars people who are later found guilty of a misdemeanor hate crime from having or carrying guns, gun ammo, stun weapons, explosives, or a hidden weapon. It applies when the assault was aimed at someone because of race, religion, gender, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, color, or national origin. A violation is a Class 1 misdemeanor, and the law takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB1015.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB1030.s: The law requires the Virginia Parole Board to complete guidelines for deciding discretionary parole for each prisoner who is eligible for parole. These guidelines are a set of rules used to help guide parole decisions. It became law and takes effect on July 1, 2027.
VA-2026-HB1030.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB1037.s: Requires Virginia's Board of Education to provide local school boards with teaching materials on climate change and environmental literacy based on peer-reviewed science. It also directs the board to create model rules for choosing those materials, including guidance to show how weather and climate change over time, how human activity affects them, and how climate change affects people and resources. The act became law and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB1037.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB1043.s: Virginia housing officials must review applications for two state housing grant programs and tell each applicant within 90 days after the deadline whether they got an award or a denial. The department must also give applicants the first notice before any public announcement and make guidelines with input from stakeholders. These rules end on July 1, 2027, and the law takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB1043.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB1046.s: Virginia law now adds new rules for some public works contracts. For construction contracts over $5 million, contractors and subcontractors must complete certain safety training, keep proof they follow the law, and get written approval before paying more than one independent contractor; local public bodies must also get a written reason for those payments. The law also calls for an 18-month study on using apprentices on public works jobs and for state agencies to publish guidance by July 1, 2027.
VA-2026-HB1046.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB1065.s: Virginia’s two biggest electric utilities would have to study how much extra power hookup room they have at some current and planned renewable power sites in the state. They would also have to run pilot programs for battery storage and solar projects that use that extra hookup room, including asking for project bids. The results would be included in their 2027 plans for new solar and onshore wind projects. It became law and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB1065.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB1100.s: The bill limits a treasurer’s lien on wages or salary for unpaid local taxes and charges to 25% of a person’s disposable earnings in one pay period. That limit would not apply in certain cases, such as when income is above 250% of the poverty guideline, when the person or property has left the area or is hiding assets, or when money was held in trust to be sent to the local government. It became law and takes effect on 7/1/2026.
VA-2026-HB1100.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB111.s: The bill would limit when local voter registrars can cancel a voter’s registration. In most cases, they could only do so based on a voter’s written request, a death certificate, or data from the state elections office or another approved state agency. It would also restore protection for some active-duty service members, people living outside the United States for a time, and their spouses or dependents.
VA-2026-HB111.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB112.s: The law makes it illegal to separate mammal babies born in captivity from their mother before they are 4 months old, unless a veterinarian says it is needed for medical care. It also bans breeding different mammal species together for commercial purposes. The rules have several exceptions, including farm animals, some zoo transfers, wildlife agencies, and emergency care, and it takes effect on 7/1/2026.
VA-2026-HB112.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB1165.s: The law changes the rules for qualifying as a division superintendent in Virginia. It requires candidates to show good character and skill as a school administrator, and it changes one path for getting a license so it includes five years of school experience, with set teaching and administration time, plus a school board recommendation from a small division. People already serving under that path keep the older rules if they stay on as a superintendent without a break. It was approved and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB1165.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB1173.s: The bill would add menopause and perimenopause to the Virginia Human Rights Act as protected conditions. It would bar discrimination in state programs, public places, hiring, and reasonable workplace accommodations for people affected by these conditions. It would also require a study on menopause and perimenopause at work and a report with best practices by July 1, 2028.
VA-2026-HB1173.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB1182.s: Health insurance plans that cover prescription drugs would have to cover FDA-approved birth control drugs and devices, including ones sold over the counter. The bill also bars copays, coinsurance, or other fees for covered prescription birth control, with some exceptions, and requires no-cost over-the-counter hormonal birth control at in-network pharmacies. It became law and takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB1182.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB1207.s: The law creates a paid family and medical leave insurance program run by the Virginia Employment Commission. It gives covered workers up to 12 weeks of paid leave for family or medical reasons, starting April 1, 2028, and lets self-employed people join if they choose. The program is paid for by premiums from employers and workers, and benefits are set at 80% of a worker's average weekly net pay, up to a statewide cap.
VA-2026-HB1207.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB1222.s: Local social services offices would have to record child welfare interviews unless they show good cause not to. It would also let any person record talks with child protective services staff during an abuse or neglect investigation or family assessment. Under current law, only a person suspected of abuse or neglect can do that recording.
VA-2026-HB1222.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB1263.s: The bill would repeal Virginia’s ban on collective bargaining by public employees. It would set up a new board to decide bargaining groups and run votes for worker representatives, and it would require public employers and those representatives to meet and bargain over pay, hours, and other work terms. It would also create a state home care council to act as the public employer for certain home care workers in collective bargaining.
VA-2026-HB1263.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB1270.s: Transportation network companies would have to send the state a private yearly report with overall data on fares, drive time, and pay for drivers on prearranged rides. They would also have to tell drivers how deactivation works, give a weekly pay summary, and send an itemized receipt within 24 hours after each ride. The law takes effect January 1, 2027.
VA-2026-HB1270.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB1273.s: As law, this measure adds new rules for ride-hailing companies and their drivers, called transportation network companies and TNC partners. It requires options for audio and video recording of rides, identity checks through the app, and tighter rules for background checks, account sharing, and who can drive. It also sets civil fines for breaking some of these rules and sends that money to the Department of Motor Vehicles. The law is effective July 1, 2026, but these parts do not take effect unless the General Assembly reenacts them in 2027.
VA-2026-HB1273.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB1279.s: Virginia law will let some religious groups and certain tax-exempt nonprofits build housing on land they own without a special permit or other extra local approval, if the project meets set conditions. At least 60% of the homes must be affordable, and they must stay affordable for at least 30 years. The homes will also be subject to local property tax after they are finished unless the locality clearly exempts them. The law takes effect January 1, 2027, and ends January 1, 2031.
VA-2026-HB1279.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB1288.s: The bill would raise the top value of property that can be sold at public auction to pay off a lien on a motor vehicle, from $12,500 to $17,000, without first asking a court for an order. It affects the process for enforcing vehicle liens. The governor vetoed it, and the House later sustained the veto.
VA-2026-HB1288.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB1377.s: A task force would be created to study higher education at Virginia Military Institute and review how the school responded to a 2021 state report. It would also look at changes to move the institute away from the Lost Cause narrative, build a more welcoming environment, and address other concerns it finds. The task force must finish its meetings by November 30, 2026, and report by the first day of the 2027 Regular Session; the law takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB1377.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB1385.s: The bill would change how public colleges and universities run their governing boards. It would extend board member terms from four years to six years and require each board to set rules for shared governance, or how different parts of the school make decisions together. It would also have the State Council of Higher Education for Virginia set up work groups to draft model shared governance rules and study legal counsel issues and recusal rules for board members.
VA-2026-HB1385.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB1392.s: The bill would change courthouse security rules for attorneys, sheriffs, and courthouse staff. If a sheriff lets courthouse employees or police skip screening, the sheriff would also have to let a lawyer in with a valid state bar card and government ID. It would also require jail phone and web systems to give prisoners a private way to talk with their lawyer, and it would make it a Class 1 misdemeanor for a lawyer with a suspended or revoked license to use a bar card to avoid screening.
VA-2026-HB1392.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB1393.s: This law changes funding for utility pilot programs that help low-income, elderly, and disabled people pay for energy help and weatherization. It requires Appalachian Power Company and Dominion Energy Virginia to keep these programs going at set funding levels, and it extends the programs until July 1, 2038. It also changes some Dominion cost rules, lets the company seek to recover certain deferred fuel costs, and adds wage and apprenticeship rules for some utility-related work; it takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB1393.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB1441.s: State and local law-enforcement agencies in Virginia would be barred from making or renewing federal immigration agreements unless those agreements include certain required terms. Officers would also be barred from using law-enforcement help or resources to aid actions to find, arrest, or punish someone for breaking federal civil immigration law, with limited exceptions for other legal authority, a valid court order, or certain custody transfers after some violent felony convictions. The measure became law as Chapter 1098 and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB1441.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB1444.s: Creates the Virginia Clean Energy Innovation Bank to help fund clean energy projects, projects that cut greenhouse gases, and other approved projects. The bank would use public money through grants, loans, and other financing tools, and an advisory board of citizen and ex officio members would oversee it. The law also sets rules for the bank's powers, lending, planning, outreach, audits, and reports, and it takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB1444.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB1450.s: The law requires insurers to give policyholders certain claims history information for all employee benefit plans. It also says this information must include pharmacy benefit claims. It became law as Chapter 1099, with a delayed effective date.
VA-2026-HB1450.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB1457.s: Virginia law now says that for some overweight commercial trucks hauling coal, the truck owner can be held responsible for the weight limit violation. The law takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB1457.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB1482.s: The law limits when law-enforcement officers may wear facial coverings while doing their official work. It allows some exceptions, such as for health or safety reasons and for officers on a special weapons and tactics team. Officers who break the rule can face discipline or a Class 1 misdemeanor, unless their agency has a written policy on facial coverings; the Department of Criminal Justice Services must also create a model policy. It became law and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB1482.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB1524.s: The law bans carrying certain assault-style guns in public streets, sidewalks, parks, and other public places, with some exceptions. It covers certain semi-automatic rifles, pistols, and shotguns, and also guns changed to work like an assault firearm. Breaking this rule is a Class 1 misdemeanor, and the law takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB1524.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB1525.s: The law adds more exceptions for people under 18 to possess or carry handguns or assault firearms in Virginia. It also makes it a Class 1 misdemeanor, which is a crime, for people under 21 to buy a handgun or assault firearm anywhere in the state. It took effect on April 22, 2026.
VA-2026-HB1525.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB172.s: The law changes how punishment is handled in criminal cases when a jury may decide it. An accused person may take back a request for the jury to set punishment until the sentencing stage starts. Lawyers may also question jurors about possible punishment to see if they can be fair during the guilt or sentencing part of the case.
VA-2026-HB172.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB196.s: The law creates a two-year pilot program to help finance mixed-income housing, which is housing for people with different income levels. The Department of Housing and Community Development, working with the Virginia Housing Development Authority, will handle loan origination and loan servicing and report its findings to the General Assembly each year by November 1. If funding is provided, it can come from up to 15% of the yearly deposit to the Virginia Housing Trust Fund. It takes effect on 7/1/2026.
VA-2026-HB196.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB2.s: This law says Virginia wants to lower heating costs for low-income residents when that can be done in a practical and cost-effective way. It requires Dominion Energy Virginia and Appalachian Power to try to provide energy-saving upgrades to at least 30% of certain households by December 31, 2031, if the State Corporation Commission finds the measures are in the public interest. The utilities must also report their work to the commission starting no later than January 1, 2028, and keep doing so each year. The law took effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB2.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB215.s: The law requires the Commissioner of Elections to get approval from the State Board of Elections before starting, ending, or changing agreements with third parties to share voter registration data. It also requires the commissioner to join and keep Virginia in the Electronic Registration Information Center, a group used for voter registration data sharing. The law took effect on 7/1/2026.
VA-2026-HB215.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB217.s: The law bans buying, selling, making, importing, or moving certain assault firearms, with some exceptions such as antique guns, guns made inoperable, and guns that use bolt, pump, lever, or slide action. It also bans the sale, import, sale, barter, transfer, or purchase of large-capacity ammo devices. Most violations are a Class 1 misdemeanor, and a person convicted under this law cannot buy, have, or carry a firearm for three years. It took effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB217.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB229.s: This law makes it a Class 1 misdemeanor to knowingly and intentionally possess certain weapons in the building of a hospital that provides mental health services or developmental services, including an emergency department or other facility giving emergency medical care. The weapons covered include firearms, knives with blades over three and one-half inches, and other dangerous weapons such as explosives and stun weapons. Hospitals must post notice of the ban at each public entrance, and some exceptions apply. The weapons may be seized by a law-enforcement officer and forfeited to the Commonwealth.
VA-2026-HB229.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB234.s: The Department of Elections would have to give each local electoral board member a standard ID badge. Board members would have to wear the badge while doing their official work on election day. A person who does not follow this rule could face a civil penalty of up to $1,000. It became law and takes effect on 7/1/2026.
VA-2026-HB234.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB238.s: The law lets workers take employers to court if they break rules on minimum wage, overtime pay, worker misclassification, or the prevailing wage rate. It also adds protection for workers who report possible legal violations in good faith, and it blocks certain retaliation for those reports. Courts may award unpaid wages, extra damages, interest, and lawyer fees, and the law takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB238.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB246.s: The bill would let some people charged with assault or assault and battery use a mental illness, brain disorder, or intellectual or developmental disability as a defense or for a lower penalty. It would affect people facing these charges, and it would require notice to prosecutors before trial if they plan to use that defense. If the evidence shows the condition contributed but does not fully excuse the conduct, a judge or jury could find the person guilty of a lesser misdemeanor.
VA-2026-HB246.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB26.s: The law creates a process for people with certain marijuana-related felony convictions or juvenile cases from before July 1, 2021, to get an automatic hearing to ask for a sentence change if they are still in jail, on probation, or under community supervision on July 1, 2026. It takes effect July 1, 2026, and ends July 1, 2029.
VA-2026-HB26.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB27.s: The bill adds domestic workers, as defined in the bill, to the rules for overtime pay. It takes effect on July 1, 2027.
VA-2026-HB27.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB281.s: The law changes rules for landlord-tenant cases over unpaid rent in Virginia. It removes a rule that had required a tenant to pay the amount the court said was due into court before using a defense. It also limits how much the court can decide in cases where a landlord seeks possession or rent while the tenant is still living in the unit.
VA-2026-HB281.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB285.s: Creates a new advisory task force in Virginia to help plan how the state uses distributed energy resources, such as small local power sources. It sets out who serves on the task force, what it can do, and requires reports to state and federal leaders. The law takes effect July 1, 2026, and ends July 1, 2027.
VA-2026-HB285.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB286.s: The law requires the Adjutant General to send a yearly report to the General Assembly on Virginia National Guard deployments, readiness, funding, and resources. It also bars the Governor from using the Guard to scare, threaten, or block people from voting, and sets limits on armed militia from other states entering Virginia for active duty. It lets certain lawmakers ask the Attorney General to review some Guard deployments and directs a work group to study how the Governor and lawmakers should respond to Guard deployments. It became law and takes effect on 7/1/2026.
VA-2026-HB286.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB290.s: The law directs the Virginia Department of Education to review how the state handles false statements about a child’s residency for school enrollment. It must work with the Virginia State Crime Commission and others as needed, then make recommendations on enforcement and penalties. The department must send a report to two legislative committee chairs by November 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB290.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB30.s: The budget bill became law and sets state spending and some revenue for Virginia for the two years ending June 30, 2027, and June 30, 2028. It covers the money in the Governor’s budget and the state programs and services that use those funds. It took effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB30.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as introduced)

VA-2026-HB308.s: Virginia law changes who oversees permits for retail tobacco sellers and liquid nicotine, moving that work from the Department of Taxation to the Virginia Alcoholic Beverage Control Authority. It also requires the board to do an unannounced buyer check at least once every 24 months to see if sellers are giving tobacco products to people under 21. Some parts take effect on October 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB308.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB312.s: Motor vehicle glass repair shops would have to give certain notices, and breaking those rules would count as a consumer protection violation. The bill also lets a car get an emissions inspection waiver if it failed inspection and its onboard diagnostic system is not ready when it is brought back for reinspection. It became law and takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB312.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB318.s: The law expands the Virginia Parole Board from up to five members to at least 11, with set appointment slots and required experience in criminal law, corrections, reentry, community services, or victim services. It also sets special parole rules for certain juvenile offenders, including a meaningful chance for release, extra factors the board must weigh, and written reasons when parole is denied or reviewed. The board must also give rehab steps to denied prisoners and review those cases each year. These board-size changes take effect July 1, 2028, and the bill became law as Chapter 1046.
VA-2026-HB318.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB320.s: A new Virginia law bars people from starting, joining, or interacting with a live stream while driving a moving vehicle on state highways, and from using an electronic device to keep that live stream going. It can also bring penalties, including license suspension, and a fine of up to $500 if the driver is in an accident at the time. The law takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB320.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB328.s: Virginia would require the Bureau of Insurance to pick a new health plan standard for 2028 or later, as allowed by federal officials. The new standard would add coverage for doula care, fertility care, hearing aids for all ages, donor breast milk, certain child mental health treatments, and treatment for polycystic ovary syndrome. The coverage rule would not apply to individual or small group plans, and the bill became law as Chapter 1048.
VA-2026-HB328.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB329.s: Virginia law now adds more types of landlord retaliation that are banned under the state rules for rentals and manufactured home lots. It also says tenants can recover actual damages and use retaliation as a defense if the landlord sues for possession. The law takes effect on January 1, 2027.
VA-2026-HB329.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB333.s: Public schools in Virginia may offer lessons on the January 6, 2021, attack on the U.S. Capitol only under set rules. The lessons and materials may not describe the attack as a peaceful protest or say there was extensive election fraud that changed or could have changed the 2020 presidential race. Any such instruction must describe it as a violent attack on U.S. democratic institutions, infrastructure, and representatives meant to overturn the election results. It became law as Chapter 1049 and takes effect on 7/1/2026.
VA-2026-HB333.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB379.s: Virginia law now requires landlords to give a prospective tenant certain written notice, or post it where the tenant can see it, before asking for or taking any payment or information. The notice must cover parts of the rental application process, including deposit and fee details. The law affects people who apply to rent homes in Virginia and takes effect on July 1, 2027.
VA-2026-HB379.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB391.s: The law changes what must be on labels for medical cannabis products, including the total and per-serving amounts of THC and CBD, and the total percentage for inhaled products. It also lets licensed cannabis businesses deliver products to a patient or the patient’s registered helper, parent, or guardian at a home, temporary home, or business, but not to places like schools, military bases, the State Capitol, or public events. It changes how long stability testing is counted for some products, and it takes effect on 7/1/2026.
VA-2026-HB391.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB395.s: Virginia now limits local rules that block small portable solar devices on homes, and it lets tenants install them in some cases. It also lets electric customers own and use these devices, and bars utilities from charging related fees or requiring approval before installation, if the bill’s requirements are met. The law also sets out some state steps on notices and safety rules, and some parts take effect on January 1, 2027.
VA-2026-HB395.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB41.s: The law changes how election officials can be removed in Virginia. The State Board of Elections may remove a member of an electoral board or a general registrar after a public hearing and a two-thirds vote, and an electoral board may remove a general registrar by a unanimous vote after a public hearing. The reasons must be neglect of duty, misuse of office, incompetence, or a clear sign the person will not do the job; some removals are final, and others can be appealed. The law takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB41.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB449.s: It would set rules for class actions, which are lawsuits brought by one or more people on behalf of a larger group. It spells out when a class case can move forward, how the court can manage it, and how settlements or dismissals can happen. It would also let these cases use the same damage rules as claims under the Virginia Consumer Protection Act, and it would take effect on January 1, 2027.
VA-2026-HB449.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB455.s: Creates rules for grants from Virginia’s opioid use reduction fund for local and regional jails that plan or run substance use disorder treatment and transition services for people in jail. Grants can last up to three years, and applicants must show how they will become financially self-supporting during that time. It became law and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB455.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB460.s: The law gives the Department of Small Business and Supplier Diversity more power to carry out changes for employment services organizations if the Governor authorizes them under existing law. It also lets the department write rules to run the program and update state rules to name employment services organizations. The law takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB460.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB483.s: The bill would create a Prescription Drug Affordability Advisory Panel to study drug costs, share reports, and suggest ways to improve price transparency and data collection. It would also let the panel ask pharmacy benefit managers for certain drug dispensing information and require annual and quarterly updates on prescription drug price trends. Drug makers and wholesale distributors would not be allowed to charge more than the federal maximum fair price for certain drugs, and violations could lead to civil penalties.
VA-2026-HB483.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB484.s: Health insurance carriers and related billing managers would have to follow set coding rules when they change a claim to a lower payment level, called downcoding. They would also have to send notice to the provider, and any dispute over a downcoded claim would need review by a real person. The law takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB484.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB5.s: Virginia law now requires most private employers and state and local governments to give paid sick leave at a rate of one hour for every 30 hours worked, with some exceptions. Workers can use it for their own illness, to care for family, or for certain needs tied to domestic abuse, sexual assault, or stalking, and they keep unused leave when they move to a new division or to a new employer in some cases. The law also lets the Labor and Industry Commissioner set rules, and it takes effect July 1, 2027.
VA-2026-HB5.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB505.s: The law says local officials who worked for a government agency controlled by their own local government are treated as having a continuing personal interest in that agency for two years after leaving the job. It also sets special rules for certain towns in Planning District 8, including suspending an officer charged with a felony, requiring a study of the town’s finances and infrastructure, and making the town adopt a plan based on that study. For those towns, it also limits votes on unposted council items and requires a full-time town manager to live in Virginia unless the council waives that rule. The law took effect on April 22, 2026.
VA-2026-HB505.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB518.s: Virginia law now requires some video streaming services, social media video services, and ad managers that reach people in Virginia to take reasonable care that short ads are not louder than the longer video they play with. The Attorney General’s office will enforce this rule. It takes effect on July 1, 2027.
VA-2026-HB518.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB547.s: The law sets pay and benefit rules for private companies that provide public bus or other transportation for a county or city. It requires those workers to get pay and benefits at least equal to similar public workers, and if the locality later runs its own transit system, it must offer those workers jobs without losing pay or benefits. These rules apply only to actions on or after July 1, 2026, and the law also calls for a state work group to study how to carry it out and report back by November 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB547.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB553.s: The Department of Corrections would have to take reasonable steps to help offenders with limited English get access to its facilities, services, programs, and activities. It would also require the department to make sure language barriers do not stop employees from communicating well with those offenders. The law took effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB553.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB561.s: The law lets a court give some people a restricted driver’s license right away if they are charged with driving while drunk, refusing a test, or certain repeat offenses, as long as an ignition interlock device is installed. An ignition interlock is a device that prevents a car from starting if alcohol is detected on the driver’s breath. It also requires a state work group to review these rules and send a report and recommendations by November 1, 2026. It became law and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB561.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB569.s: State agencies and local governments would have to require workers on public works jobs paid with public money to be paid at least the local prevailing wage rate. The bill also changes which projects count as public works, includes some higher education work, and sets rules for how the labor commissioner figures out wage rates. Contractors that break the wage rule could face damages, and interested people could challenge contract terms that do not follow the law. It became law and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB569.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB61.s: The bill would create a state program to raise the use of certified small SWaM businesses in procurement by executive branch agencies and covered institutions. It would set goals for spending, require some purchases to be set aside for small SWaM businesses or microbusinesses, and create a new division in the Department of Small Business and Supplier Diversity to help carry out these efforts. It would also require a new disparity study every five years to look at the gap between the number of women-owned and minority-owned businesses and how often they are used.
VA-2026-HB61.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB614.s: Virginia will require the Department of Education to review the state history and social science standards, curriculum guides, and related materials. The goal is to make sure they include clear and accurate teaching about the roles and contributions of all peoples. The department must send a report on its findings by November 1, 2028.
VA-2026-HB614.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB627.s: This law adds health care professionals to the workers who cannot be bound by a noncompete, which is a promise not to work for a competing employer. It covers people licensed, registered, or certified by the Board of Medicine, Nursing, Counseling, Optometry, Psychology, or Social Work. An employer that breaks this rule can be fined $10,000 for each violation. It takes effect on 7/1/2026.
VA-2026-HB627.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB630.s: The law expands ranked choice voting to any local governing body, not just county boards of supervisors and city councils. It directs the State Board of Elections to set standards, approve vote-counting software, make voter education materials, and allow needed recount changes, and it lets localities ask for risk-limiting audits. It also requires the Department of Elections to review voting equipment testing and approval and report back by the first day of the 2027 Regular Session, and it makes ranked choice voting a permanent option.
VA-2026-HB630.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB636.s: The law bars employers from asking job seekers for their past pay or using that past pay to decide whether to hire them or what to pay them. It also requires pay ranges to be shown in job and promotion postings and sets a legal claim for workers or applicants who are harmed. An employer that breaks these rules can owe damages, legal fees, and other relief, and the law takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB636.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB637.s: The bill would make it a crime to possess an item with residue of a controlled substance and set different penalties based on the offense. It would affect people found with residue on an item, not just a usable amount of the drug.
VA-2026-HB637.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB639.s: The bill would let election offices accept property, services, money, or grants from private people or groups to help pay for voter education, outreach, voter registration, or other election costs. Gifts or grants over $1,000 would need approval by a two-thirds vote of the State Board of Elections or the local governing body. It was vetoed by the Governor.
VA-2026-HB639.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB640.s: The law ends the process that let a voter challenge another voter’s right to vote at a polling place on election day. It also ends a process where three voters could challenge a voter’s registration before the local election official, but such challenges can still be filed in circuit court. It became law and takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB640.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB642.s: The bill would set up a retail marijuana market in Virginia and assign it to the Virginia Cannabis Control Authority. It says retail sales could not start before January 1, 2027. Starting that same date, oversight of retail sales of some regulated hemp products would move from the Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services to the Virginia Cannabis Control Authority. The bill was vetoed by the Governor.
VA-2026-HB642.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB650.s: The bill would bar certain federal civil immigration enforcement actions in some protected places, including courthouses, some polling places, and certain state-owned health care, school, higher education, and prosecutor offices. It would also forbid civil arrests in a courthouse under a civil administrative warrant, with some exceptions for child support orders and arrests tied to a court case, and it would allow a judge-issued warrant or subpoena. Local school boards could add a way to notify staff and parents about immigration-related activity on school grounds, and public colleges would have to require a judge-issued warrant or subpoena before someone can enter nonpublic campus areas for immigration enforcement.
VA-2026-HB650.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB670.s: The law changes how Virginia labor rules apply to the state, its agencies, local governments, and other public bodies. It says those groups can count as an "employer" for certain worker protection rules, and it defines "public body" for labor and employment laws. It became law as Chapter 1065.
VA-2026-HB670.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB675.s: The law bars employers, including state and local government, from using threats or pressure based on a worker's immigration status to violate wage laws. A worker can file a complaint with the Commissioner of Labor and Industry within 180 days, and the commissioner can investigate and fine the employer. Penalties can be up to $5,000 for the first violation, $9,000 for the second, and $12,000 for later ones. It takes effect on 7/1/2026.
VA-2026-HB675.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB678.s: For landlords who own more than four rental units, it requires written notice of any rent increase for the next lease term at least 90 days before the term ends. The notice must also give the tenant a deadline, at least 30 days after the notice is sent, to say whether they will renew, and the law takes effect on Jan. 1, 2027.
VA-2026-HB678.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB702.s: Local police departments in counties, cities, and towns may set up firearm give-back or buy-back programs by January 1, 2028, and every year after that. The bill also sets rules for those programs, requires annual reports to the State Police, and says money from sold or auctioned guns must go to the local general fund or program costs. It became law and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB702.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB711.s: Ground-mounted solar projects of 1 megawatt or more on farm, business, industrial, or institutional land would have to follow local rules on things like setbacks, fences, panel height, views, grading, and cleanup plans, unless they are already allowed by right. Local governments would also have to send special exception decisions and reasons for any denial to the State Corporation Commission, which would keep a public searchable list for at least five years. The new rules apply to applications filed on or after July 1, 2026, and the law took effect on that date.
VA-2026-HB711.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB768.s: The law lets a circuit court or district court order a custody evaluation to help decide custody or visitation for a minor. It also asks the state psychology board, with the state medical board, to lead a study on the supply of qualified mental health experts who can serve in family court cases and report back by November 1, 2026. The act became law and takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB768.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB77.s: State and local police in Planning District 8 would be allowed to enforce federal traffic violations on any highway in that area. The law takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB77.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB773.s: Changes the rules for absentee voting by giving local election officials more time to fix mistakes in absentee ballots and ballot applications. It removes one deadline tied to when ballots must be received and moves the deadline to fix application errors to noon on the Monday after the election. It became law and has a delayed effective date of September 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB773.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB774.s: The law changes the process for fixing mistakes on absentee and provisional ballots. Voters who have a problem on a provisional ballot form must be told by phone or email and given a chance to fix it by noon on the Monday after the election. It also moves the deadline to fix absentee ballot application errors to that same Monday and tells the state election office to give local officials guidance on handling and counting provisional ballots. It became law with a delayed effective date of September 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB774.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB796.s: The law changes how Virginia regulatory boards set fees. It ends some required fee cuts or refunds when a board has extra money, and lets boards in the professions and health fields review fees each year so they cover costs but are not too high. It also lets these boards charge some people up to $500 or $1,500 in reasonable costs tied to investigations, discipline, and checks on compliance. The law takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB796.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB820.s: The bill creates a two-year pilot program to help finance mixed-income housing, which is housing for people with different income levels. The Department of Housing and Community Development and the Virginia Housing Development Authority would run the program and report its findings to the General Assembly each year by November 1. If funded, the program would use up to 15% of the annual deposit to the Virginia Housing Trust Fund, and it takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB820.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB834.s: Virginia landlords must take extra steps before ending a rental after a fire or other damage. They must try to meet with the tenant, offer a similar unit if one is open, or decide the tenant caused the damage by not caring for the unit as required by law. If the tenant asks after notice, the landlord must look again at the damage and whether the unit can still be lived in, unless the landlord already found the tenant caused the damage. It became law and takes effect on January 1, 2027.
VA-2026-HB834.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB848.s: Changes the rent-escrow rules for tenants who sue a landlord over major problems under Virginia’s landlord-tenant law. It removes the rule that all rent must be put into escrow before relief can be granted, and instead requires rent that comes due to be paid into escrow within five days of the due date while the case is pending, unless a court changes that amount. Missing an escrow payment on time would not end the case, but a court could consider it when making an order. It became law and takes effect on January 1, 2027.
VA-2026-HB848.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB857.s: This law says a court must assign a pregnant person or a postpartum person who still has contact with their infant child to a home/electronic incarceration program for certain offenses, unless there is probable cause to believe the person will not appear in court or would pose an unreasonable danger to the person, their family or household members, or the public. It also says a pregnant or postpartum person in this program can still be eligible for bond.
VA-2026-HB857.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB86.s: The bill would set up a mattress recycling program in Virginia. It would let certain industry groups run the program with state approval, and it would require mattress producers, retailers, and renovators to register and follow program rules. It would also require a plan before the program starts, plus yearly reports and state oversight.
VA-2026-HB86.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB871.s: The law requires a person who keeps a firearm in a home where a minor or someone barred from having a gun is present to store the gun and ammunition in a locked container, compartment, or cabinet that the person cannot reach. A person who breaks this rule commits a Class 4 misdemeanor. Gun dealers must also post a written notice about the penalty, and the law takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB871.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB872.s: The law requires each chief judge in district and circuit courts to set rules for visitors on bringing and using portable electronic devices, like phones or tablets. The judge can set limits on how they are used or carried in the courthouse. These rules must be posted at the courthouse entrance and also made available online. It became law and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB872.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB888.s: The law limits how much off-street parking local governments can require for some home, apartment, and mixed-use projects in certain designated areas. In those areas, they cannot require more than 0.5 parking spaces per apartment or mixed-use home unit, or more than 1 space per unit for single-family, two-family, and townhouse homes. In localities with more than 20,000 people, the law also requires a process to cut minimum parking rules by at least 20% for similar projects outside those areas. It took effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB888.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB891.s: Battery storage projects tied to approved solar sites would be allowed as a permitted extra use in all zoning areas if they stay within the parcel and meet safety and environmental rules. Local governments could not require another local land use approval for those projects, but they could still enforce codes and safety rules. For some projects with an interconnection request filed before July 1, 2030, the local rules in place on July 1, 2026, would apply. Became law and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB891.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB892.s: Virginia passed a law that requires Dominion Energy to give the State Corporation Commission more information about how it forecasts its power needs and meets renewable energy rules in its resource plan. It also orders the Commission to start a review by March 1, 2027, of load forecasting practices at Dominion Energy, Appalachian Power Company, and electric distribution cooperatives. The law takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB892.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB909.s: The law extends rules that limit certain conduct at polling places to places where people can vote absentee in person. It also bars most people from knowingly carrying a gun within 100 feet of the entrance to polling places and certain other election sites. The law took effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB909.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB925.s: The law changes the time limit for filing an employment discrimination complaint under the Virginia Human Rights Act to two years from the date of the alleged act, instead of 300 days. It also lets a person start a civil case after 180 days if the complaint was filed with a local human rights commission. The law took effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB925.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB931.s: The law sets rules for recovery homes and tells the state to set minimum certification standards for them. It says a recovery home cannot require a person to use medical or mental health services, including substance use treatment, if the home gets money from those services. State agencies and courts may refer people only to certified recovery homes, and the state must watch the groups that give out these credentials to make sure they follow the rules.
VA-2026-HB931.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB95.s: Virginia enacted a change to landlord-tenant law that affects landlords with more than four rental units or a large stake in them. Before ending a lease for nonpayment of rent in certain cases, the landlord must give written notice of the exact amount due and offer a payment plan to pay it in monthly parts. While the tenant follows that plan on time, the landlord may not add new late fees for that unpaid rent. It became law and takes effect on July 1, 2027.
VA-2026-HB95.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB952.s: The bill would let certain industrial stormwater permit holders use nutrient credits from the Chesapeake Bay watershed program to meet nutrient reduction rules for 2025 and 2026, if they meet set conditions. It would also direct the Department of Environmental Quality to focus on enforcement when permit holders do not meet those rules and to form a work group to study future compliance rules. The law takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-HB952.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB964.s: The law restores voting rights to some people when they are released from incarceration after a felony conviction, and lets them register to vote. It also tells state agencies to share release information and give people voter registration forms and release papers when they leave. The law also updates the rule for people found unable to understand voting, and it takes effect January 1, 2027, if the related constitutional changes are approved.
VA-2026-HB964.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HB972.s: Virginia would change how voter rolls are checked and updated. It requires the Department of Elections and local registrars to use certain ID matches, send notice before canceling a voter’s registration, and keep cancellation records that are public. It also limits how federal SAVE data and out-of-state voter data can be used, and some parts would start on July 1, 2027.
VA-2026-HB972.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-HJ315.s: The resolution would call for the election of circuit court judges, general district court judges, and juvenile and domestic relations district court judges in Virginia. It passed both the House and the Senate.
VA-2026-HJ315.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as introduced)

VA-2026-HJ4001.s: Sets limits on the kinds of bills the 2026 Special Session I of Virginia's General Assembly may consider and sets a schedule for its business.
VA-2026-HJ4001.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as introduced)

VA-2026-HR106.s: The House agreed to a resolution honoring the life and legacy of Mildred Delores Jeter Loving.
VA-2026-HR106.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as introduced)

VA-2026-HR139.s: The resolution encourages the U.S. Navy to choose Naval Air Station Oceana in Virginia Beach as the home base for new F-35C fighter squadrons. The F-35C is a stealth strike fighter used by the Navy. The House agreed to it.
VA-2026-HR139.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as introduced)

VA-2026-HR205.s: This resolution would formally recognize the legacy of Laurel Grove School. It affects the school’s history and legacy, not a program or rule change.
VA-2026-HR205.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as introduced)

VA-2026-HR2052.s: A House resolution about salaries and other basic office expenses for the House of Delegates.
VA-2026-HR2052.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as introduced)

VA-2026-HR2069.s: The House agreed to a resolution that would limit what legislation can be considered during the 2026 Special Session I of the General Assembly. It would also set a schedule for how business is handled in that special session.
VA-2026-HR2069.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as introduced)

VA-2026-HR2070.s: The House resolution would commend Mount Calvary Baptist Church for its 150th anniversary.
VA-2026-HR2070.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as introduced)

VA-2026-HR24.s: The House resolution would name people to be elected to circuit court judge seats in Virginia. It affects the judge election process in the circuit courts.
VA-2026-HR24.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as introduced)

VA-2026-HR25.s: The House adopted a resolution nominating people to be elected to general district court judgeships. It affects the people who would be put forward for those court seats.
VA-2026-HR25.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as introduced)

VA-2026-HR26.s: This resolution would name people to be elected as judges for juvenile and domestic relations district courts. It affects the nominating process for those court seats in Virginia.
VA-2026-HR26.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as introduced)

VA-2026-HR27.s: The resolution would nominate a person to be elected as a member of the State Corporation Commission. It affects that state agency position. The House agreed to it and elected the nominee.
VA-2026-HR27.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as introduced)

VA-2026-HR28.s: The House would nominate a person to be elected to the Virginia Workers' Compensation Commission. It is a formal step in choosing a member for that state commission. The House agreed to it by voice vote and elected it on January 21, 2026.
VA-2026-HR28.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as introduced)

VA-2026-HR4.s: The resolution expresses support for Virginia taking part in the Southern Regional Education Board’s Crisis Recovery Support Network. It affects the state’s role in that support network.
VA-2026-HR4.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as introduced)

VA-2026-HR428.s: The resolution would commend Jamie Harless for his work with Lord Botetourt High School football. It is a formal statement of recognition from the House.
VA-2026-HR428.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as introduced)

VA-2026-HR483.s: This resolution would nominate people to be elected as circuit court judges. It affects the process for filling circuit court judgeships in Virginia.
VA-2026-HR483.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as introduced)

VA-2026-HR484.s: The House resolution would nominate people to be elected as general district court judges. It affects the selection of judges for those courts in Virginia.
VA-2026-HR484.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as introduced)

VA-2026-HR485.s: The House resolution would name people to be elected to juvenile and domestic relations district court judgeships in Virginia. It affects the process for filling those judge positions in that court.
VA-2026-HR485.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as introduced)

VA-2026-HR6.s: The House of Delegates resolution would set the rules for how the chamber runs during the 2026-2027 sessions of the Virginia General Assembly. It affects House members and the way House business is handled during those sessions.
VA-2026-HR6.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as introduced)

VA-2026-HR7.s: The House of Delegates resolution deals with salaries and other expenses, including contingent and incidental costs.
VA-2026-HR7.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as introduced)

VA-2026-SB106.s: Virginia law now sets civil fines for a retail store that sells, gives, or hands out a tianeptine product without a prescription. The fine is $2,500 for the first violation and $5,000 for a second or later violation within three years. The law takes effect on 7/1/2026.
VA-2026-SB106.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB107.s: The law lets certain caregivers ask to be excused from jury duty. It covers a person who has legal custody of a child under 18 with a serious health condition, and a family caregiver of someone with a serious health condition. It became law and takes effect on 7/1/2026.
VA-2026-SB107.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB125.s: The law changes the Office of the Children's Ombudsman’s powers and duties. It gives the office more access to certain records and reports, lets it send some complaints to the Office of the Inspector General, and changes some reporting rules and definitions. When asked, the office must report findings and recommendations about state agencies failing to protect children to the Governor or the General Assembly. It takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB125.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB126.s: The bill changes filing rules for a primary election when an incumbent office holder misses the deadline to file paperwork to get on the ballot. In that case, the filing deadline is extended by five days for other people running for the office. It became law and takes effect on January 1, 2027.
VA-2026-SB126.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB128.s: The law adds health care professionals to the workers covered by Virginia’s ban on noncompete deals, which are agreements that limit where someone can work after a job ends. It applies to people licensed, registered, or certified in medicine, nursing, counseling, optometry, psychology, or social work. Employers that break this rule can be fined $10,000 for each violation. It takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB128.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB137.s: This law creates a Class 1 misdemeanor for a person who uses force, threats, or physical obstruction to intentionally injure, intimidate, or interfere with someone getting or providing "reproductive health services." It also covers a person who intentionally damages or destroys, or tries to damage or destroy, a "reproductive health care facility" because it provides those services. The law says it does not restrict the content of any message a person may want to communicate.
VA-2026-SB137.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB162.s: The law restores voting rights for some people when they are released from incarceration after a felony conviction, and lets them register to vote. It also requires state agencies to share release information and give people voting forms and instructions when they are released. It changes the rules for people found unable to understand voting, and takes effect January 1, 2027, if the related constitutional amendments are approved in the November 3, 2026 election.
VA-2026-SB162.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB17.s: The bill would raise the highest value of property that can be sold at public auction to pay a lien on a motor vehicle without first asking a court for permission, from $12,500 to $17,000. It would affect people trying to enforce liens on motor vehicles in Virginia.
VA-2026-SB17.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB173.s: This law makes it a Class 1 misdemeanor to knowingly bring a firearm, a knife with a blade over three and one-half inches, or another dangerous weapon into the building of a hospital that provides mental health services or developmental services in Virginia, including an emergency department or other emergency care facility. It also requires notice of the ban to be posted at each public entrance. The law allows certain exceptions and says the weapon may be seized and forfeited to the Commonwealth.
VA-2026-SB173.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB176.s: The law expands ranked choice voting, which lets voters rank choices, from some local races to any local governing body. It also sets rules for ballot software, damaged ballots, voter education, recounts, and optional audits for these elections. The Department of Elections must review voting equipment rules and send a report by the first day of the 2027 Regular Session. It takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB176.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB181.s: Allows local governments to give a partial property tax break for buildings turned into homes, if part of the space is set aside for lower-income households or tied to an affordable housing agreement. Localities can decide who qualifies, what rules apply, how big the tax break is, and how long it lasts, up to 15 years. If a building later stops meeting the rules, the locality can take back some or all of the tax break, and a buyer may face a penalty if the property no longer qualifies after a sale. The bill became law and takes effect on 7/1/2026.
VA-2026-SB181.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB197.s: Virginia's flood fund loan and grant program would pause loan interest and delay repayment for localities and federally recognized or Virginia recognized tribes using the money for flood prevention projects or studies in areas that flood often. The pause would last until the project or study is finished. It became law and takes effect on 7/1/2026.
VA-2026-SB197.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB199.s: Virginia law sets paid sick leave rules for private employers and state and local governments, with some exceptions. Workers would earn 1 hour of paid sick leave for every 30 hours worked, and certain workers paid by fee-for-service would earn leave under state rules. The law also lets workers use sick leave for some domestic abuse, sexual assault, or stalking needs, and it allows penalties and lawsuits if an employer breaks the rules. It became law and takes effect July 1, 2027.
VA-2026-SB199.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB2.s: The law creates a paid family and medical leave insurance program run by the Virginia Employment Commission. It provides up to 12 weeks of paid leave for covered workers, funded by premiums paid by employers and employees starting April 1, 2028. Self-employed people may choose to join, and benefits start April 1, 2028; the law takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB2.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB215.s: This law bars a future employer from asking for a job applicant’s past pay or using that pay when deciding whether to hire or how much to pay. It also requires pay or pay ranges to be shown in job and promotion postings, and it protects workers and applicants from retaliation for asking about pay ranges or not sharing past pay. A person harmed by a violation can sue for damages, legal fees, and other relief, and the law takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB215.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB218.s: The bill would require the Department of Corrections director to keep taking and reviewing requests to house inmates from states that are part of the Interstate Corrections Compact, a compact that lets states share prison space. It would also stop any of those inmates from being placed at Red Onion State Prison unless the General Assembly later gives that approval again. The bill was vetoed by the governor.
VA-2026-SB218.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB223.s: Creates a task force in the executive branch to help guide Virginia’s move toward distributed energy resources, which are smaller power sources like solar and battery systems. It sets out the task force’s members, powers, and duties, and requires reports to state and federal officials and certain lawmakers. The law takes effect July 1, 2026, and ends July 1, 2027.
VA-2026-SB223.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB225.s: Creates the Virginia Clean Energy Innovation Bank to help fund clean energy projects, projects that cut greenhouse gases, and other qualified projects. The bank would use public money through grants, loans, credit help, and other financing tools, and an advisory board of citizen and ex officio members would oversee it. It became law and takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB225.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB226.s: Local governments could give a tie-breaking preference to compost products made in the same locality when buying them. A locality could also require some large waste producers to separate organic waste, such as food scraps, and keep it out of final disposal, with civil penalties after a warning. The measure also states that new or updated public school buildings should include trash, recycling, food scrap, and liquid waste disposal areas.
VA-2026-SB226.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB229.s: This bill would set rules for class actions, which are lawsuits brought by or against a group of people with similar claims. It would spell out when a class case can be filed, how a court certifies it, what lawyers must do, and how settlements or dismissals can happen. It would also let class cases use the same damage rules as Virginia Consumer Protection Act cases and would take effect on January 1, 2027.
VA-2026-SB229.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB23.s: Starting July 1, 2026, plea deals and court orders would not be able to include terms that take away a defendant’s rights against unlawful searches, or the right to ask for expungement or sealing of records. Any such term would be void and unenforceable, with some limited exceptions in certain cases. The bill also limits how long a search-right waiver can last: no longer than the supervised probation period, or up to five years if there is no supervised probation.
VA-2026-SB23.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB230.s: This law lets some people ask to clear police and court records tied to an arrest or charge if they were not convicted or found responsible in the end. It also covers some juvenile and traffic cases, some deferred cases, and some protective orders, and it sets rules for how courts handle objections and missing records. It takes effect on December 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB230.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB24.s: The law requires the Commonwealth, when asked by the accused or their lawyer, to make copies or photos of discovery materials they can inspect, such as police reports, criminal records, dashboard camera footage, and body camera footage. Those copies must follow court rules on redaction and limited sharing, and some items may not be distributed if the law bars it. It also directs a state agency to study and report on the costs and other effects of giving defense counsel police reports at least 10 days before trial or a preliminary hearing. It became law and takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB24.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB250.s: This law lets people use small portable solar devices on homes if they meet certain rules. It also lets tenants install them in some cases, stops local governments and certain utilities from blocking them, and bars utilities from charging fees or demanding approval before use. The law also tells a state agency to create a notice form and a state office to study safety rules, and some parts start on January 1, 2027.
VA-2026-SB250.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB253.s: Virginia's law changes funding for pilot programs that help low-income, elderly, and disabled people pay for energy needs and weatherize homes. It keeps those programs going through July 1, 2038 and sets annual funding ranges for Appalachian Power Company and Dominion Energy Virginia. It also lets Dominion Energy Virginia seek recovery of certain approved costs, changes some rate rules for large business customers, and allows a petition for securitizing certain deferred fuel costs. The law takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB253.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB256.s: The law sets minimum energy and water saving standards for certain appliances and HVAC equipment if federal standards are removed. It says new products in Virginia could not be sold, leased, or rented unless they meet those standards, and it lets the state energy department adopt rules tied to the last federal standards in place by December 31, 2025. It also leaves out products where a court has set aside a standard or federal law controls the rules.
VA-2026-SB256.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB258.s: The bill would ban discrimination under Virginia’s Human Rights Act based on menopause or perimenopause in government programs, public places, hiring, and requests for reasonable help from an employer. It would also require the Labor and Industry and Health commissioners to study menopause and perimenopause at work and make best-practice guidance. The report would go to the Governor and General Assembly by July 1, 2028, and be posted online.
VA-2026-SB258.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB270.s: Recovery homes would have to meet new state certification rules. The bill also says people in these homes could not be forced to take medical or mental health services as a condition of living there if the home gets paid for those services, and state agencies and courts could refer people only to certified homes.
VA-2026-SB270.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB271.s: The bill would create a prescription drug advisory panel to study drug prices, make policy ideas, and report on pricing trends each year and each quarter. It would also require pharmacy benefit managers, which help run drug plans, to share some drug use data with the panel on request. Drug makers and wholesale sellers in Virginia would be barred from charging more than the federal maximum fair price for certain drugs, and violations could bring civil penalties of $10,000 per violation or, in some cases, $100,000 or more.
VA-2026-SB271.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB28.s: This law adds domestic workers, as defined in the bill, to the state rules on overtime pay. It applies to workers covered by those overtime rules. The law takes effect on July 1, 2027.
VA-2026-SB28.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB285.s: The Department of Housing and Community Development must review and set rules for the Urban Public-Private Partnership Redevelopment grant program. The rules must give priority to local areas with high fiscal stress or a big drop in commercial real estate values, and must address both money and other kinds of local match help. The department must report its findings to certain legislative committees by November 1, 2026, and the law takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB285.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB324.s: The law adds new rules for some public works contracts in Virginia. It requires contractors and subcontractors to finish certain safety training and keep records showing they follow the law. For contracts over $5 million, it adds written approval and notice rules before paying more than one independent contractor, and it also calls for a study on using apprentices on public works jobs.
VA-2026-SB324.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB335.s: The bill would let a person use mental illness, a neurocognitive disorder like dementia, or an intellectual or developmental disability as a defense, or to get a lower penalty, in some assault cases. It would also require advance written notice before trial if that defense is used. If the defense does not fully apply but the condition still played a part, the case could be treated as a Class 1 misdemeanor.
VA-2026-SB335.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)
