VA-2026-SB337.s: The law requires the Adjutant General to send lawmakers a yearly report on Virginia National Guard deployments, plus details on retention, readiness, funding, and resources. It bars the Governor from using the Guard to scare or stop people from voting, and it limits when armed militia from another state may enter Virginia for military duty without the Governor’s consent. It also lets some lawmakers ask the Attorney General to review certain Guard deployments and directs a work group to study how state leaders should respond to Guard deployments.
VA-2026-SB337.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB342.s: If land with a conservation or open-space easement is taken by condemnation, the person taking it would have to pay the Commonwealth and the local government for certain tax credits and other values listed in the bill. Any payment to the Commonwealth would be in addition to other required compensation. It became law and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB342.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB344.s: The law makes it illegal to separate a baby mammal born in captivity from its mother before the baby is four months old, unless a veterinarian says it is needed for medical reasons. It also bars breeding mammal species together on purpose for commercial use. The rules do not apply to farm animals, certain zoo transfers, some wildlife agency and rescue work, or emergency care; it takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB344.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB347.s: Local governments will have to use set rules when reviewing large ground-mounted solar projects on land zoned farm, business, industrial, or public use, unless the project is already allowed by right. Those rules can cover things like setbacks, fences, panel height, visual impact, grading, and a plan to remove the equipment later. Localities must send solar special-exception decisions to the State Corporation Commission, which will keep a searchable public list of those decisions for at least five years. The law applies to projects filed on or after July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB347.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB348.s: In Virginia, people who keep a firearm in a home with a minor or someone who cannot legally have a gun would have to lock up the gun and its ammo in a locked container, compartment, or cabinet that the other person cannot reach. A person who breaks this rule would be guilty of a Class 4 misdemeanor. Gun dealers would also have to post a written notice about this penalty, and the law takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB348.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB351.s: The bill would limit certain federal immigration enforcement actions in some protected places, including courthouses, polling places, hospitals, schools, and certain state offices. It would bar civil arrests in a courthouse based on a civil administrative warrant, with some exceptions, and would allow arrest or access when supported by a judicial warrant or judicial subpoena. It would also let local school boards add a notice step to school safety plans and require public colleges to set a rule for people doing immigration enforcement work before they can enter nonpublic campus areas.
VA-2026-SB351.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB352.s: The law says Virginia police officers may not wear face coverings while doing their official work, with some exceptions such as medical protection and special weapons teams. Officers who break the rule can face discipline, and in some cases a Class 1 misdemeanor, unless their agency has a written policy on face coverings. It also tells the Department of Criminal Justice Services to make a model policy for agency use. The act became law and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB352.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB361.s: Health insurance plans that cover outpatient prescription drugs would have to cover FDA-approved birth control drugs and devices, including ones sold over the counter. People using prescription birth control could not be charged a copay, coinsurance, or fee in most cases, and plans that cover hormonal birth control would have to offer over-the-counter options at in-network pharmacies with no cost-sharing. The law was approved and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB361.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB364.s: This bill directs the Secretary of Public Safety to convene a work group to develop policy and legislative recommendations to establish the Virginia "Gun Violence Prevention Center." The work group may meet in person or virtually, use small group breakouts, and collaborate with experts and other representatives as needed. It must report its findings and any legislative and policy recommendations to the General Assembly by December 15, 2026.
VA-2026-SB364.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB378.s: The bill would have ended Virginia’s ban on collective bargaining by public employees. It would have set up a new board to handle bargaining units and elections, and would have required public employers to bargain in good faith over pay, hours, and other work terms. It also would have created a Virginia Home Care Council to act as the public employer for certain home care providers in collective bargaining. The bill was vetoed by the governor.
VA-2026-SB378.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB388.s: Passed law that lets certain religious and nonprofit tax-exempt groups build housing on land they own with normal zoning approval, instead of needing extra local permits or special reviews. At least 60% of the homes must be affordable, and the housing must stay affordable for at least 30 years. The housing is generally subject to local property tax after it is finished unless a locality exempts it. It takes effect on January 1, 2027, and ends on January 1, 2031.
VA-2026-SB388.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB398.s: The law makes several changes to the Virginia Birth-Related Neurological Injury Compensation Program and Fund. It lets certain injury claims go to the Virginia Workers' Compensation Commission, allows claims to be filed online, adds payment for an education advocate, and raises the award limit for families from $100,000 to $500,000. It also changes who serves on the board, requires monthly board meetings, and says the Fund must pay for some commission filing system costs and certain audit review work. It takes effect on 7/1/2026.
VA-2026-SB398.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB425.s: Starting July 1, 2026, cities with more than 20,000 people and counties with more than 100,000 people would have to consider adding an environmental justice plan when they review their comprehensive plan. The plan would identify environmental justice and fenceline communities and set goals to lower health risks, support public input, and focus local programs on those communities. It would also call for baseline environmental and health data to help spot uneven health conditions.
VA-2026-SB425.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB429.s: Virginia law now requires nursing homes to tell the resident, the resident’s family, and the Department of Health if a required doctor visit does not happen. Nursing homes must also do a full yearly assessment of each resident, review it at least every 92 days, and review it sooner if the resident’s health changes a lot. The law also tells the Health Department and the State Health Commissioner to work on better care, stronger oversight, staff training, and an annual report on nursing home quality. It takes effect on 7/1/2026.
VA-2026-SB429.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB43.s: The law directs the Virginia Department of Energy to study demand response programs, which help manage power use when demand is high. It must look at the benefits, impacts, best practices, and ways to put these programs in place across the state. The department must send a report by November 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB43.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB433.s: The law changes Virginia’s unemployment rules for workers locked out by an employer. If a worker is otherwise eligible, they can get benefits unless their union refuses to meet with the employer under reasonable conditions, has been found under federal law to bargain in bad faith, or the lockout came from the union breaking an existing contract. It became law as Chapter 890 and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB433.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB436.s: The law limits photo speed cameras in highway work zones to times when workers are present. It also changes what proof counts in a speed case from those work zones unless the camera operator gives a sworn note that workers were there. It takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB436.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB438.s: In-person absentee voting would have to be offered for at least five hours on the second and third Sunday before all elections, between 11:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. This affects voters who use absentee voting in person. The law takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB438.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB439.s: The bill changes who serves on the advisory committee and work group for the College and Career Ready Virginia Program by removing the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond from both groups. It became law and takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB439.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB443.s: This law says battery storage projects tied to approved solar farms are allowed in all zoning areas on that land if they stay within the parcel and follow safety and environmental rules. Local governments may not require extra local land-use approval for those projects, though they can still enforce safety codes and work out a siting agreement. For some projects with an interconnection request filed before July 1, 2030, the local rules in place on July 1, 2026, will apply. It became law and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB443.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB446.s: Virginia law extends how long certain limited-duration licenses, driver privilege cards, permits, and identification cards stay valid, with some limits for REAL ID and commercial driver documents. It also updates the rules for some limited-duration commercial driver licenses and ties them to federal rules. The Department of Motor Vehicles must use the new longer time periods when these documents are renewed or reissued, and the law takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB446.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB447.s: Creates the Virginia Boys and Men Advisory Commission in the state legislature. The commission would advise lawmakers on issues that affect boys and men in Virginia, including school gaps, job chances, health outcome gaps, and social media use. It became law on April 13, 2026, and includes an emergency clause, which means it took effect right away.
VA-2026-SB447.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB448.s: The law raises the energy storage goals that Appalachian Power and Dominion Energy Virginia must ask state regulators to approve, with set targets for short- and long-term storage by 2040 and 2045. It also tells the Department of Energy to work with other state agencies to write sample local rules for energy storage projects by December 1, 2026. The State Corporation Commission must also run a test program for long-duration energy storage, review safety standards, and decide by March 1, 2031, whether the new targets are workable.
VA-2026-SB448.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB450.s: Virginia’s Department of Education must bring together a stakeholder work group to review alternative paths to teacher licensure for public school teachers. The group must study how these paths work and make ideas to improve their quality and results. The department must send an interim report by October 1, 2026, and a final report by October 1, 2027. The measure became law and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB450.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB453.s: The law sets a civil penalty of up to $50,000 for each violation for anyone who intentionally discharges untreated sewage onto land or into waters in Virginia. It applies to people who do this kind of sewage discharge and takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB453.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB459.s: Liquefied petroleum gas fitters would have to give customers a written offer, within 14 days of a request to stop gas delivery, to remove any gas left in the tank and pay the customer back at the going rate. If the customer accepts, the fitter would have to do that within 30 days. Breaking these rules would count as a violation of the Virginia Consumer Protection Act. It became law and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB459.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB47.s: The law makes it a Class 6 felony to pretend to be a law-enforcement officer while committing or trying to commit certain violent sex crimes or while getting past a security measure at certain buildings. A second or later offense is a Class 5 felony. It became law and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB47.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB479.s: Changes are made to Virginia rules for stock corporations, including how boards can delegate share-issuance duties and how some shareholder agreements are kept on file. The law also lets a corporation keep a vote on a matter before shareholders even if the board later changes its mind about supporting it. It became law and takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB479.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB487.s: Electric cooperatives may set up a virtual power plant program, which means a group of small energy sources working together to help the power grid. They may give rewards to home customers who buy battery storage devices and must look at ways to better manage power demand. The bill became law and takes effect on 7/1/2026.
VA-2026-SB487.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB489.s: Virginia now requires virtual currency kiosk operators to get a license from the State Corporation Commission. Operators must file regular reports, give certain notices, and take steps to help stop fraud and money laundering. The law also sets daily and monthly transaction limits, caps fees at 18% of the transaction value, and can fine violators up to $1,000 per violation. It takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB489.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB490.s: The law creates a two-year pilot program for mixed-income housing. The Department of Housing and Community Development, working with the Virginia Housing Development Authority, would handle loan setup and servicing for these projects and report to the General Assembly each year of the pilot. Any funding would come, if approved, from up to 15% of the yearly deposit to the Virginia Housing Trust Fund. It takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB490.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB491.s: Virginia law now says public schools cannot deny a child a free public education through high school because of the child’s or parents’ real or perceived immigration or citizenship status. It also bars school boards, schools, school resource officers, and school staff or contractors from taking certain actions that would block access to school programs or benefits for that reason. The law creates a way for people to sue over violations and requires state guidance, local school policies, and training for school leaders.
VA-2026-SB491.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB493.s: The law changes rules for automatic renewals and continuous service offers, which are plans that keep charging until you cancel. It says sellers must give clear notice and a cancellation way that is at least as easy to use as signing up, and it changes some words and definitions in the current law. Some businesses lose an old exemption, and breaking these rules counts as a consumer protection violation. It became law and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB493.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB494.s: The bill would change how public college and university governing boards are set up. It would make board member terms six years instead of four and require each board to set rules for how shared decision-making works at the school. It would also have the state higher education council set up work groups to draft model rules and study legal counsel issues and when board members must step aside from a vote because of a personal, money, or partisan or ideological interest. The bill was vetoed by the Governor.
VA-2026-SB494.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB495.s: The law expands who can ask a court for an emergency substantial risk order and adds factors a judge or magistrate must consider when deciding whether to issue one. It also shifts these cases to lower courts as well as circuit courts, sets rules for cases involving minors, and explains how firearms that belong to someone else must be returned. A false statement made during the petition process can be charged as a Class 1 misdemeanor, and the law takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB495.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB496.s: The law says a handgun left in an unattended vehicle must be stored in a locked hard-sided container, such as a locked glove box or center console. It creates a Class 4 misdemeanor for failing to do that, with some exceptions, including reporting a theft or loss to police as required by law. It became law and takes effect on 7/1/2026.
VA-2026-SB496.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB5.s: The law creates a task force to look at barriers to energy-saving programs for people with lower incomes and to study how state agencies can work together better. The group must meet at least six times between July 1, 2026, and September 30, 2027, and turn in a report by September 30, 2027. Its report must also include policy ideas and a plan to help provide weatherization repairs and whole-home energy upgrades to eligible households in the state by December 31, 2034.
VA-2026-SB5.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB504.s: The law says a landowner’s vested rights in a specific residential project cannot be changed by a later local circuit court ruling on a zoning rule change if that ruling affects at least 25 parcels in a locality. That protection does not apply if the court ruling is directly about the government action that approved the project. It took effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB504.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB506.s: Clear film could be put on a vehicle’s windshield if it is kept in line with federal rules. The change applies to vehicle equipment rules in Virginia. It became law and takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB506.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB508.s: The law requires Appalachian Power and Dominion Energy Virginia to study how much extra interconnection capacity is available at their existing and planned intermittent power sites in Virginia. It also directs them to set up pilot programs for energy storage and solar projects that use this extra connection space, including a request for proposals. The results of those requests must be included in their 2027 plans for new solar and onshore wind power, and the law takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB508.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB513.s: The bill lets two state agencies update the written crisis-services plan after it is published, as long as listed stakeholders are consulted and the public gets at least 30 days to comment. That plan would be the guide for parts of Virginia’s crisis system and the Marcus alert system, and state and local partners would have to keep their rules and work in line with it. It became law and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB513.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB515.s: The law renames the Commission on Electric Utility Regulation as the Energy Commission of Virginia. It became law and takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB515.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB516.s: Virginia law now requires investor-owned electric utilities and electric cooperatives to send monthly reports on residential power shutoffs to the State Corporation Commission. The reports must include details like shutoffs for nonpayment, how long it took to reconnect service, unpaid balances, and whether affected homes use payment help or have a serious medical condition form on file. The Commission must post the data in an easy-to-use online database and send a yearly summary to the Governor and the Commission on Electric Utility Regulation, starting by September 1, 2027.
VA-2026-SB516.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB518.s: The law requires state agencies and local governments to make sure public works contracts paid with public money include pay at least equal to the local prevailing wage. It also changes what counts as public works, adds some higher education work, and bars the definition from covering certain broadband or telecom work on non-government property. Contractors or subcontractors can face damages for breaking the wage rule, and people with a stake in the project can challenge contracts that do not follow it.
VA-2026-SB518.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB522.s: The Office of Working Lands Preservation in the Department of Forestry would also manage the Forest Sustainability Fund. The measure affects that office and the state forestry department. It became law as Chapter 824 and takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB522.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB524.s: The law requires health plans to use network rules for mental health and substance abuse care that set clear standards for timely access, travel time, and distance. It also changes how insurers must submit federal parity reviews, lets the insurance bureau act on bad reports, and updates the bureau’s yearly report to lawmakers. The health plan parts take effect July 1, 2027.
VA-2026-SB524.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB527.s: Creates a grant fund to give money to a qualified company that makes pharmaceutical substances and signs an agreement with Virginia. The company must be expected to invest at least $4 billion and create and keep at least 500 new full-time jobs. The grants can be paid from July 1, 2026, through July 1, 2045, with limits on yearly and total amounts.
VA-2026-SB527.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB531.s: This law requires local zoning rules for single-family areas to allow accessory dwelling units, or ADUs, as a permitted added home. People must get a local permit, and the fee must be $500 or less if they meet the listed rules. Localities also cannot make the ADU setback rules or other size and frontage rules stricter than those for single-family homes in the same area, and they cannot require family ties between occupants. It takes effect July 1, 2027.
VA-2026-SB531.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB532.s: This law lets certain alcohol makers and sellers sponsor or provide support for a special event when a municipality or nonprofit organization has a banquet license. The event must be held on the grounds of a museum or a government-registered national, state, or local site where the municipality or nonprofit organization runs a gift shop, and any retail license for the premises must be deactivated during the event. It also limits those municipalities or nonprofit organizations to no more than eight banquet licenses for these events each year.
VA-2026-SB532.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB536.s: Requires medical malpractice insurers and certain hospitals and health systems in Virginia to report yearly data on premiums, claims, payments, legal costs, and financial condition. It also requires them to report how many doctors and other health workers are covered, their malpractice costs, and any jury verdicts above the state recovery cap. The reports must go to certain lawmakers by September 1, 2026, for 2025 data, and by March 31 each year after that for the prior year. Became law and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB536.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB542.s: The bill would set up a retail marijuana market in Virginia and put the Virginia Cannabis Control Authority in charge of it. No retail sales could start before January 1, 2027. Starting that same day, oversight of some regulated hemp products would move from the state agriculture agency to the Cannabis Control Authority.
VA-2026-SB542.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB543.s: The law increases enforcement and penalties for the illegal sale of marijuana and marijuana products by certain licensed businesses. It also requires retail marijuana stores to display a state decal that lets shoppers check the store’s license, and it sets civil penalties for not displaying it or for making a fake one. It also lets the Cannabis Control Authority order people to stop unlicensed marijuana activity, seize illegal marijuana products, and creates a work group to study efforts against illegal cannabis sales and report by October 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB543.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB550.s: Ride-hailing companies would have to send the state a private yearly report with group data on fares, drive time, and driver earnings. They would also have to tell drivers about the deactivation process, give them a weekly earnings summary, and send an itemized receipt within 24 hours after each ride. The law was approved and takes effect on January 1, 2027.
VA-2026-SB550.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB553.s: This law requires certain water users that report water withdrawals to also report monthly amounts of potable water and reclaimed water they give to others offsite. It applies to data centers with an air permit, and, when possible, to domestic, commercial, industrial, and other uses. It takes effect on January 1, 2027.
VA-2026-SB553.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB57.s: Requires the Commissioner of Elections to apply for, join, and keep Virginia in the Electronic Registration Information Center, a voter registration data-sharing group. This would affect state election officials who handle voter list maintenance. It became law and takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB57.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB575.s: The bill changes a state purchasing law to leave out certain federal intergovernmental support agreements from a construction rule under Virginia’s public buying system. That rule lets a public body buy from another public body's contract when the bid or proposal said the purchase was a joint buy for other public bodies. It became law and takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB575.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB582.s: Virginia would change how absentee and provisional ballots are handled after an election. Local officials would have to quickly tell voters by phone or email about mistakes on a provisional ballot form and give them a chance to fix them by noon the Monday after the election; the same deadline would also apply to fixing certain absentee ballot application errors. The law also requires daily updates on absentee ballot status, gives voters free online access to that information, and takes effect September 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB582.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB583.s: This law lets local governments allow transit agencies to use bus obstruction monitoring systems. The systems can help enforce local rules against parking, stopping, or standing in bus stop zones or in lanes set aside for buses during posted times. It became law and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB583.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB59.s: The law lets retired law enforcement officers, registered special conservators of the peace, and local technicians sign or affirm papers used to prove certain traffic and school bus camera violations, if they finish a training course. It also requires law enforcement officers who do this work to complete that training. The training must be ready by January 1, 2027, and these rules take effect July 1, 2027.
VA-2026-SB59.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB594.s: Virginia law now bars auto insurers from automatically adding a person to a motor vehicle owner's policy, or to the named insured's household for that policy, based only on certain listed information. It affects insurance carriers that can write motor vehicle liability policies and people insured under those policies. It became law and takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB594.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB595.s: The bill changes how the DMV looks up owner or lienholder records for some vehicles titled in another state. It removes one step the DMV had to take in some mechanic's lien, storage lien, and abandoned vehicle cases, but keeps the lookup when the person holding the vehicle starts the search. It became law and takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB595.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB597.s: Limits a local treasurer’s wage garnishment for unpaid taxes and charges to 25% of a person's take-home pay in one pay period. That limit would not apply in some cases, such as when the person's income is above a set poverty-line level or when the treasurer has clear proof the person is leaving the area or hiding assets. It became law and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB597.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB599.s: Virginia made changes to how grants are given from a fund that supports substance use disorder treatment and transition services in local and regional jails. The grant rules must now allow awards for up to three years, and applicants must show how they will become financially self-supporting during that time. The law takes effect July 1, 2026 and affects local and regional jails that seek this funding.
VA-2026-SB599.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB60.s: Virginia changed the size and makeup of the Parole Board, raising it from up to five members to at least 11, with set picks from the Governor, the House speaker, and the Senate rules chair. It also gives certain juvenile offenders a clearer chance at parole review and requires the board to weigh youth, maturity, rehabilitation, and public safety when deciding. If parole is denied, board members must explain their reasons, give recommendations for rehabilitation, and review those cases each year; the board changes take effect July 1, 2028.
VA-2026-SB60.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB600.s: The bill changes how nonjudicial discipline works in the Virginia National Guard. It removes a rule that had stopped demotion in rank for members with more than 10 years of service who are E-5 or higher. It became law and takes effect on 7/1/2026.
VA-2026-SB600.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB612.s: Virginia extended the motion picture production tax credit through taxable year 2030 instead of 2026. The credit helps film and TV productions that meet the state's rules. The bill became law and takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB612.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB62.s: The law creates a process for some people with marijuana-related felony offenses, or related probation or supervision violations, to get an automatic hearing to ask for a sentence change. It applies to offenses committed before July 1, 2021, for people still in jail or under supervision on July 1, 2026. The law takes effect July 1, 2026, and ends on July 1, 2029.
VA-2026-SB62.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB620.s: Creates a permit system for retail tobacco product sellers, moving oversight from the Department of Taxation to the Virginia Alcoholic Beverage Control Authority. It also requires the authority to do undercover buyer checks at least once every 24 months to see if permit holders sell tobacco products to people under 21. Some parts take effect on October 1, 2026, and it became law as Chapter 1021.
VA-2026-SB620.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB621.s: Virginia law now requires Dominion Energy and Appalachian Power to ask the State Corporation Commission to approve grid use measures by October 15, 2026. Their filings must compare how the electric grid is working now with how well it could use existing power lines and other assets. The Commission must also add its findings to an existing yearly report, including whether each utility could use more non-wires alternatives, like other ways to meet power needs without building new wires. The law takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB621.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB637.s: The law expands the Virginia Human Rights Act so that educational institutions count as places of public accommodation for nondiscrimination rules. It also lowers the number of workers needed for an employer under job discrimination rules from 15 to 5, and gives people two years instead of 300 days to file a discrimination complaint with the Attorney General’s office. It took effect on 7/1/2026.
VA-2026-SB637.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB64.s: The bill creates a process for the Department of Juvenile Justice to ask a court to extend a juvenile's stay in its care beyond the usual guideline period. The department must file the request at least 60 days before that period ends, and the court would hold a hearing and then decide whether to release the juvenile or extend the commitment for up to six more months. It became law and takes effect on 7/1/2026.
VA-2026-SB64.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB640.s: The law creates a central hotline for reports and complaints of child abuse or neglect, and local complaints must be sent to that state hotline. It gives the Commissioner of Social Services power to require a corrective action plan for local social services offices that do not follow the law or that put a child or adult at substantial risk, and in some cases to take over part or all of a local office. The law also adds adult services to the meaning of social services, and the hotline changes take effect July 1, 2027.
VA-2026-SB640.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB645.s: The law changes a permit rule for a small renewable energy project in Planning District 8. It lets some electric facilities that run on biomass, energy from waste, or municipal solid waste count if they can use anaerobic digestion, a process that breaks down organic waste without air, for most of their food waste and sludge by January 1, 2030. It also directs the Department of Environmental Quality to study ways to cut carbon dioxide and methane at waste-to-energy plants, look at ways to make biomethane, and report its findings by December 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB645.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB648.s: The law changes ethics rules for local governing body members who worked for a local government agency they oversee, treating that agency as a continuing personal interest for two years after they leave the job. It also adds special rules for certain towns in Planning District 8, including suspending an officer charged with a felony, requiring a study of the town’s debt and other risks, and making the town adopt a plan to address those needs. For those towns, it also limits council votes on items not posted ahead of time and requires a full-time town manager to live in Virginia unless the council waives that rule.
VA-2026-SB648.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB658.s: The law directs the Department of Elections to form a work group to study how to set up back-end, opt-out automatic voter registration in Virginia. The group must include state agencies, lawmakers, local election officials, and voting rights and data privacy groups, and it will compare the new setup with the current process and look at costs and benefits. The Secretary of Administration must send a report to the House and Senate election committees by November 1, 2026. It became law as Chapter 590 and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB658.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB659.s: The law creates a grant program to help public bodies pay for costs tied to connecting solar projects to the power grid. Grants are given on a competitive basis, and solar sites on already developed land get priority. The state energy office will run the program, set its rules, and the law takes effect July 1, 2026, with the program ending July 1, 2027.
VA-2026-SB659.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB660.s: The law creates a process for self-storage facility owners to dispose of an occupant’s personal property if it is left behind after a rental ends or is not renewed, as long as the problem was not about unpaid money. It also allows the renter’s last known address to be updated in a way the rental agreement says. The law became Chapter 951 and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB660.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB661.s: The bill would set rules for electronic skill game devices in Virginia, including how they are registered, licensed, made, sold, operated, hosted, and played under the Virginia Lottery’s oversight. It would also add a 25% tax on the gross profits from play of these devices and place the money into a new fund for commerce and development. The bill would also create criminal and civil penalties for breaking the law or the rules for these devices.
VA-2026-SB661.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB666.s: The law requires the Department of Housing and Community Development to gather housing development data from each local government and share it in one public database. The database must be machine-readable and work with screen readers, and it must include data on new and existing housing developments, how many plans were submitted and approved, and the average time for plan review. It became law and takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB666.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB67.s: The law lets any locality, by local rule, allow certain local workers and police officers to give out parking tickets for parking, stopping, and standing violations. Before, only localities with at least 40,000 people could do this. It became law as Chapter 938 and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB67.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB680.s: The law changes how certain Virginia licensing boards can set fees. It lets boards under the Department of Professional and Occupational Regulation and the Department of Health Professions adjust fees each year, and it lets them charge some people up to set amounts for investigation and discipline costs. The agencies must report fee changes each year, and the law takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB680.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB685.s: Virginia school boards must create, follow, and post a language access plan on their websites for parents with limited English. The plan must help make sure these parents can communicate well and get information they can understand, and the law takes effect July 1, 2027.
VA-2026-SB685.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB690.s: The law removes the need for the Department of Criminal Justice Services to create a model addiction recovery program for local and regional jails. That program could have been used by sheriffs, jail officers, and jail leaders. It became law as Chapter 828 and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB690.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB693.s: Motor vehicle insurers in Virginia would not be allowed to deny coverage, limit coverage, or charge a different rate for the same coverage only because of a person's consumer credit info or credit-based insurance score. The bill also directs the State Corporation Commission’s Bureau of Insurance to study how insurers use that information when setting policies and to report its findings and recommendations by October 1, 2027. It became law and takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB693.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB70.s: The law lets a court send a delinquency case back to the court service unit before the hearing starts, if the child asks and the attorney for the Commonwealth agrees. If that happens, the court must dismiss the petition and erase the court record for that case. It also lets intake officers handle some child welfare and delinquency complaints informally again in some cases where that was limited before. It took effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB70.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB706.s: The Department of Health must keep a list of agencies and groups that ask for and get opioid blockers through its distribution program. It must also send quarterly reports on how the blockers are given out, and each year by December 1 it must estimate the program’s costs for the next fiscal year. The law takes effect July 1, 2026 and applies to the department and the lawmakers listed in the report rules.
VA-2026-SB706.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB707.s: The law makes it unlawful for a veterinarian to do a surgical devocalization on a dog, which is a surgery to change how a dog barks or makes sound. It allows the surgery only when it is needed to treat an injury, disease, or birth defect that is causing, or may cause, physical pain or harm. It took effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB707.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB713.s: The law clarifies that when a local court is inside another county, city, or town’s courthouse, certain local sheriffs and police officers can use their full police powers there and on nearby courthouse property. It also lets them enforce certain state laws while at the courthouse or while traveling to and from it for official duties. It became law and takes effect on 7/1/2026.
VA-2026-SB713.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB719.s: The law requires the Secretary of Agriculture and Forestry to create and put into action a written Virginia Farm and Forest Prosperity Plan during the first year of each new governor’s term. The plan is meant to be carried out over that governor’s term. The secretary must also give a progress report to the governor and two legislative committees by December 1 of that first year.
VA-2026-SB719.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB72.s: Virginia law says the state should try to lower heating costs for low-income residents when it is practical and cost-effective. Dominion Energy Virginia and Appalachian Power must make reasonable efforts by December 31, 2031, to provide energy-saving upgrades and related improvements to at least 30% of certain eligible homes, if the State Corporation Commission says the work is in the public interest. The companies must also send reports to the Commission starting no later than January 1, 2028, and the law took effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB72.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB724.s: Now law, this measure says any new or changed high school graduation rules or diploma paths must apply only to students who start ninth grade in the first school year when the new rules are used or later. It applies starting with students who enter ninth grade on or after the 2027-2028 school year.
VA-2026-SB724.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB725.s: Virginia’s circuit court clerks will charge a higher Technology Trust Fund Fee, from $5 to $8. The law changes how that fee is split, lets $2 go to each clerk’s office for allowed uses, and removes the recordation tax for certain quitclaim deeds and correction deeds when no money changed hands. It also requires clerks to report fee money collected and spent, and for a state report to be sent by December 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB725.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB727.s: A law in Virginia bars people from carrying certain assault-style firearms in public areas, like streets, sidewalks, parks, and other places open to the public, with some exceptions. It also covers some firearms changed to work as assault firearms. Breaking the rule is a Class 1 misdemeanor. The law takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB727.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB73.s: The law directs the state Medicaid agency to train local school staff on how to handle Medicaid billing for certain services provided in schools. It is meant to help school divisions understand the rules and use Medicaid funding for student health services. It became law as Chapter 816 and takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB73.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB731.s: Private companies that provide public transit for a county or city would have to pay their workers at least as much, and give them at least the same benefits, as similar public workers. If a local government later starts its own transit system, it would have to set rules for collective bargaining and offer those private-company workers jobs without losing pay or benefits. The law also sets up a work group to study how to carry it out and report by November 1, 2026, and it applies to actions on or after July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB731.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB734.s: The law lets the State Corporation Commission approve, after a request, one person to serve as an officer or board member for more than one financial institution. The Commission must find that the institutions do not compete with each other, or that one or both might otherwise lack capable management from someone who lives or works in the area they serve. It became law and takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB734.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB744.s: The law lets public recreational facilities authorities give grants to local governments, state and federal agencies, other public bodies, and other people to support the authority’s goals. That includes grants for tourism development. It became law and takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB744.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB748.s: The law expands the process for a court order that clears certain records for people who were victims of human trafficking. It adds related matters, arrests, and charges tied to qualifying offenses, and it broadens the list of offenses that can qualify. It takes effect on 7/1/2026.
VA-2026-SB748.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB749.s: The law bans the purchase, sale, transfer, import, and making of assault firearms and certain large-capacity ammo devices, with some listed gun types left out, such as antiques and guns run by bolt, pump, lever, or slide action. It makes these acts a Class 1 misdemeanor, and a person convicted under it cannot buy, have, or move a firearm for three years. It became law and takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB749.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB75.s: Virginia law now updates rules for moving people in emergency custody or temporary detention. It says retired law-enforcement officers can count as law-enforcement officers for these cases, and it lets certain alternative transport workers move a person safely, including some state or private hospital staff and workers for the state behavioral health agency or its contractors. For minors, it sets when an alternative transport worker counts as available, and says custody stays with that worker until the minor reaches the temporary detention facility. The law took effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB75.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB753.s: The law expands Virginia’s rules on using a person’s name or image without permission to also cover a person’s voice or likeness. It keeps the same kind of lawsuit, remedies, and time limit for these cases. It applies to people whose voice or likeness is used without permission, and it takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB753.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB756.s: The bill would add Fairfax County to the list of places that can host a casino in Virginia. Any casino site in Fairfax County would have to be near a Metro Silver Line station, part of a large mixed-use project, close to a large enclosed mall, and outside the Interstate 495 Beltway.
VA-2026-SB756.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB759.s: Starting July 1, 2026, people who qualify for unemployment benefits will get $48 more each week than the current amount. It applies to unemployment claims that begin on or after that date.
VA-2026-SB759.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB764.s: The bill would let a court delay the final decision in some criminal cases and, in some cases, suspend a driver's license for 10 days to 6 months. For drunk driving cases, it would let the court require an alcohol safety program and block driving unless the car has an ignition interlock device, which is a device that checks for alcohol before the car starts. It would not apply to people with a commercial driver’s license or permit, or to those driving a commercial vehicle in the alleged offense. It was vetoed by the governor.
VA-2026-SB764.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB767.s: The law adds notice rules for motor vehicle glass repair shops and makes breaking those rules a consumer protection violation. It also lets a vehicle get an emissions inspection waiver if it failed inspection and its onboard diagnostic system is not ready to be tested at reinspection. It became law and takes effect on 7/1/2026.
VA-2026-SB767.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB771.s: This law raises the workers' compensation burial expense payment from $10,000 to $15,000. Starting January 1, 2028, the amount for burial and reasonable transportation costs will be adjusted each year based on the rise in the U.S. Consumer Price Index, and it affects employers that must make these payments.
VA-2026-SB771.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB776.s: The law changes how courts handle a probationer who does not pay fines or court costs. A missed payment alone does not count as a probation violation unless the court finds, after notice and a hearing, that the person willfully refused to pay. Courts must assume a person who is legally indigent cannot pay, and the law took effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB776.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB777.s: Electric utilities and licensed electricity suppliers that join or set up the regional transmission group PJM Interconnection would have to file a yearly report with the State Corporation Commission by February 1. The report would list votes they cast, votes cast by their affiliates, and a short note on why each vote was in the public interest. The rules would not apply to city-run utilities or certain electric co-ops, and the law takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB777.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB779.s: Virginia's law on eminent domain changes how money is paid in condemnation cases. The circuit court clerk must give out just compensation and any interest within seven business days after the court order or after the money is received, whichever is later. It also lets lawyers ask for a copy of the jury panel and requires the certificate to be filed with the clerk on the same day it is recorded in the land records.
VA-2026-SB779.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB783.s: Law-enforcement agencies in Virginia would have limits on their agreements with federal immigration authorities. It would also bar officers from using local resources to help with operations to find, arrest, or punish people for federal civil immigration law violations, with some listed exceptions. The bill became law and takes effect on 7/1/2026.
VA-2026-SB783.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB784.s: The law bars bioslurry injection, a way of putting slurry into a well, in any well drilled through part of a groundwater management area set by rule before January 1, 2020. It applies to people using those wells in Virginia. It became law as Chapter 833 and takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB784.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB785.s: School boards must report each year the number and type of teacher, instructional, and support staff exits in their schools, broken down by race. They must also report the reason for each exit, including whether it was voluntary or involuntary. It became law and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB785.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB788.s: The bill changes how beer, wine cooler, and wine excise taxes are reported and paid, and sets new penalty limits for late filing or payment. It gives manufacturers, bottlers, wholesalers, and retailers up to 60 days to fix the problem before a license can be suspended or revoked, if they file the return, pay the tax, submit reports, and pay any penalty. It also requires the Virginia Alcoholic Beverage Control Authority to set up an online system for wholesale wine licensees to report monthly sales and tax collected by January 1, 2027. It became law and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB788.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB790.s: Health insurance plans in Virginia would have to cover medically necessary care and treatment for menopause and perimenopause. The rule applies to certain individual and group health insurance policies, subscription contracts, and health maintenance organizations, which are plans that provide health care services. It became law and takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB790.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB794.s: The law sets up rules for Virginia law officers and courts around protected health care activity, meaning certain health care actions that are legal in Virginia. It bars state and local officers from investigating, arresting, detaining, or helping with cases over that activity, and it lets people sue for court orders if those rules are broken. It also limits extradition to other states for some related charges and requires some out-of-state subpoenas and witness summonses to say whether they involve that activity.
VA-2026-SB794.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB800.s: The Winchester Parking Authority would get the power to sell, lease, transfer, or otherwise dispose of property or property rights it has acquired. This affects the Authority and the property it owns or controls, and the law was approved as Chapter 956, effective July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB800.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB801.s: Virginia removed the old designation of "Carry Me Back to Old Virginny" as the state's official song emeritus. The change affects the state song designation and became law, taking effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB801.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB802.s: Virginia agencies would have to set up and run a market-based trading program to cut carbon dioxide from power plants. The program would follow the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative rules already in state law. It became law as Chapter 921 and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB802.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB803.s: Virginia’s Fair Housing Board would have to write rules that define terms tied to unlawful conduct under the state fair housing law, including quid pro quo harassment and hostile environment harassment. It would also have to use emergency rules to put the changes in place. The measure became law and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB803.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB804.s: The law changes how the Judicial Inquiry and Review Commission’s yearly report can be changed before it is made public. It says a group of committee leaders from the House and Senate must agree before any part of the report is taken out or blacked out. If no changes are made, the report must be published within 30 days after it is sent to the General Assembly, with the time extended for weekends, legal holidays, or days when the legislature is closed.
VA-2026-SB804.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB81.s: State and local police in Planning District 8 would be allowed to enforce federal traffic infractions on any highway there. The law applies to officers in that part of Virginia. It became law and takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB81.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB812.s: The law makes the state pay medical fees for anonymous trace evidence kit exams for victims who report strangulation. These victims do not have to join the criminal case or work with police to get the exam. It also tells the state workers' compensation commission to make rules for paying these exams and calls for a work group to study and report on the reimbursement process by November 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB812.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB813.s: The bill creates the Sickle Cell Coordinated Access Network. It directs the State Health Commissioner and Virginia Commonwealth University Health Systems Authority to set up and run the network so health care providers in Virginia can get real-time advice and support from sickle cell specialists. It became law and takes effect on July 1, 2027.
VA-2026-SB813.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB818.s: Virginia law now lets some large nonresidential electric customers of Appalachian Power or Dominion Energy Virginia buy power from a licensed supplier if their peak demand was over five megawatts last year. It also shortens the advance notice needed to switch back to the utility from five years to 18 months. The law takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB818.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB822.s: School districts in Virginia would have to make sure school nurses take training on sickle cell disease within six months of starting work and then at least every three years. The course could be online or in person, and it must be approved by the state board with the Health Department. The measure became law and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB822.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB823.s: The law gives the Board for Contractors power to set rules for contracts and disclosures for residential solar energy deals, including sales, leases, and power purchase agreements. These contracts must include certain details about the solar company, system performance or output guarantees, and invoices and payments. It also allows a civil penalty of up to $2,500 for each willful violation and takes effect on January 1, 2027.
VA-2026-SB823.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB827.s: The bill expands Virginia’s pilot program for underground power lines and lets the State Corporation Commission fast-track and approve up to four new qualifying projects filed between January 1, 2025, and July 1, 2033. A project must meet set cost, technical, and local support rules, and at least half of certain added undergrounding costs must be paid by the local area through a levy, bonds, local funds, or a mix of these. It also pushes the pilot program’s final report deadline to December 1, 2034. It became law and takes effect July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB827.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB83.s: The bill would require chief judges of district and circuit courts to set rules for visitors’ portable electronic devices, such as phones and tablets. It would also set security rules for courthouses, create a misdemeanor for a suspended or revoked lawyer who tries to use a bar card to skip screening, and require jails to give lawyers better ways to meet and talk with clients. It also would require local jails to provide a phone, online, or web-based way for prisoners to contact attorneys.
VA-2026-SB83.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB832.s: The law directs the Virginia Department of Transportation to set up criteria and make recommendations for marking certain areas as vulnerable road user safety zones, where crashes, injuries, or deaths involving people walking or biking have been high. It also requires the department to send a report with those criteria and any recommendations to key Senate and House committees by November 1, 2026, and it takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB832.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB84.s: The law lets state and local police use camera systems to record some pedestrian crossing and stop sign violations in school crossing zones, highway work zones, and high-risk speed corridors. It also sets rules for how these devices are used, how summonses are issued, and how records and penalties are handled. In some highway work zones, the devices can be used only when workers are present.
VA-2026-SB84.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB88.s: The bill requires people civilly committed to a state-run residential behavioral health facility to be counted and assigned for redistricting and reapportionment. It became law as Chapter 552 and takes effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB88.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SB98.s: Virginia made a law that directs the Secretary of Public Safety and Homeland Security to create a work group to study emergency management needs in the state. The group must look at how current funding is working and review other funding models used in other states. It must report its findings and suggestions to lawmakers by October 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SB98.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as passed)

VA-2026-SJ1.s: This constitutional amendment would say every individual has a fundamental right to abortion and that the state may not deny, burden, or infringe on that right unless it meets a strict test. It would allow the Commonwealth to regulate abortion care in the third trimester. It would also say the Commonwealth may not prohibit an abortion if a physician says it is needed to protect the pregnant person's life or physical or mental health, or if the fetus is not viable.
VA-2026-SJ1.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as introduced)

VA-2026-SJ2.s: This constitutional amendment says people who meet Virginia’s voter rules have a basic right to vote, and that right cannot be taken away by law except in two cases: people convicted of a felony and people a court has found unable to understand voting. People serving time for a felony would not be able to vote while in jail, but their voting rights would return when they are released without needing more action. People found unable to understand voting would not be able to vote until their ability is restored under the law. It became law and takes effect on 7/1/2026.
VA-2026-SJ2.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as introduced)

VA-2026-SJ3.s: Virginia amended its constitution to remove the old rule that marriage is only between one man and one woman. It says two adult people can get a marriage license and have their marriage recognized, no matter their sex, gender, or race. The law took effect on July 1, 2026.
VA-2026-SJ3.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as introduced)

VA-2026-SR2001.s: Sets the operating rules for Virginia’s 2026 Special Session I of the legislature.
VA-2026-SR2001.src: Virginia Division of Legislative Services summary (summary as introduced)
